summary:
Tunceli stands under the national framework of Turkey. No trans-specific statute, enforcement pattern or incident documentation specific to Tunceli was identified in the source inventory; this absence is recorded as absence of documented divergence rather than as evidence of local permissiveness, and the national assessment applies.

At the national level, a leaked omnibus reform draft known as the 11th Judicial Package, reported by Human Rights Watch on 29 October 2025, would amend the Turkish penal code to punish conduct "contrary to biological sex" with up to three years in prison, and participation in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony with up to four years. The draft would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care including surgery from 18 to 25, mandate permanent infertility and repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals, and expose both healthcare professionals performing such care and patients to criminal prosecution, with pretrial detention possible. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association opposed the draft, and Human Rights Watch called for its withdrawal. Whether the package has since passed is unresolved in the sources.

Kaos GL's Human Rights Report 2025, titled "The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People," finds that LGBTI+ hostility became explicit state policy, with instructions issued to public institutions under the "Year of the Family" banner. The report documents 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings, with trans people the most affected; 89 torture or ill-treatment violations, a striking increase over the prior year; 313 right-to-liberty violations, about 2.5 times the previous year, comprising 299 detention decisions; freedom-of-expression violations rising from 216 to 540; and 40 right-to-association violations including the first closure of an LGBTI+ association in many years.
tangentialFactors:
The 11th Judicial Package draft sits within a broader authoritarian drift in Turkey, and the Erdoğan government has repeatedly used "the family" and "public morals" framing to legitimise stigmatisation of LGBT people.

Raw counts in the Kaos GL report track national monitoring coverage rather than per-capita rates; the year-on-year multiples (right-to-liberty violations at roughly 2.5 times the prior year, freedom-of-expression violations rising from 216 to 540) are the more reliable signal of direction of travel than absolute totals.
localsOnly:
Trans residents of Tunceli live under the same national legal and policing regime documented country-wide: facilities organised by registered sex rather than gender identity, arbitrary body and strip searches for LGBTI+ detainees, de facto isolation, restricted healthcare, and no policy or staff training to identify LGBTI+ needs. Hormone replacement therapy is not covered by the government healthcare system and must be obtained and paid for privately.

Turkey has no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on sexual orientation or gender identity, and no direct discrimination protection for gender identity; the European Commission's 2025 report found legal protection insufficient and out of line with the EU acquis.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted since Human Rights Watch's 29 October 2025 report is unresolved in the sources.

No source in the inventory documents Tunceli-specific policing, incidents, facilities practice or official statements toward trans people; the absence of such documentation is not evidence that none exist.
